The Raising of Lazarus

Icons

Feasts

The Raising of Lazarus

Lazarus Saturday · Lazarus of Bethany

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

John 11:1–45

John 11:25–26

King James Version · Scripture previews

St. Nicholas parish places Lazarus Saturday immediately before Holy Week and pairs it with Palm Sunday. The published account reads the raising of Christ’s friend as assurance before the Passion and an anticipation of the universal resurrection.

[1] Introduction; Biblical Story, final two paragraphs

What is depicted

Christ calls toward the tomb while Lazarus emerges still wrapped in burial cloths. Mary and Martha bow before Him. Disciples and other witnesses surround the event; the removed stone and the walled city complete the explanation’s account of the composition.

[1] Icon of the Feast, paragraphs 1–3

History and tradition

The selected fifteenth-century icon is identified as work of the Novgorod school from the Kirillo-Belozersky Monastery, now in the Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg. This historic panel is a different artwork from the modern icon illustrated on the parish’s page.

[2] File description and displayed historic reproduction

Published explanation

The parish explains that Christ’s tears for His friend manifest His humanity, while His command over the dead manifests divine power. Its interpretation joins grief and victory rather than treating Lazarus’s return simply as an isolated marvel.

[1] Biblical Story, final two paragraphs

Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

[3] John 11:25
